shellRuntime.f836: How should a Leo make use of a good day?

shellRuntime.f900: What are the trine and the clash in the Rat reading?
shellRuntime.f901: A trine (三合) is a set of three branches that lift each other's force. The Rat (Zi) forms the Water trine with the Monkey (Shen) and the Dragon (Chen). shellRuntime.f910: Does the animal reading change every day?

shellRuntime.f912: Yin (寅) is the force of wood as spring begins. Those born in the Year of the Tiger cannot stand injustice and force open what is blocked. Having little fear, they go first down roads others cannot take.

shellRuntime.f916: Should a Tiger be careful on a day that carries a clash?

shellRuntime.f918: How does the animal reading differ from Four Pillars?
shellRuntime.f919: The animal reading uses only one branch — that of your birth year — while Four Pillars uses all four pillars of year, month, day, and hour. The animal reading suits looking at the broad flow; Four Pillars suits looking at an individual's concrete board.
shellRuntime.f920: Mao (卯) is the wood of spring in full. Those born in the Year of the Rabbit are soft and finely tuned, and they arrive where they want without colliding. Their aesthetic sense is strong and they put people at ease.

shellRuntime.f928: Chen (辰) is the end of spring, earth holding water. Those born in the Year of the Dragon work at scale and are good at enlarging the board; staying in an ordinary place feels stifling. The amplitude of their fortune is wide, so the rises and falls are pronounced too.
shellRuntime.f929: Their presence is strong and they make opportunities big. In a crisis their judgement turns bold.

shellRuntime.f931: Break a big goal down into one step you can take today. When the first step is concrete, the Dragon's execution follows.
shellRuntime.f932: Why is the Dragon said to have wide swings of fortune?
shellRuntime.f933: Chen (辰) is earth holding water — a branch where forces of different natures gather in one place. So a smooth flow and a blocked one tend to divide sharply, and the interpretation shows a wide amplitude as well.
shellRuntime.f934: Why do results differ between people born in the same Dragon year?

shellRuntime.f940: Is there a reason the money axis matters for the Snake?

shellRuntime.f944: Wu (午) is the fire of midsummer. Those born in the Year of the Horse send their energy outward and cannot bear being shut in. They brighten the mood among people, and the more they move the more fortune attaches to them.

shellRuntime.f946: With a foot in several places, nothing ripens. Pour your time into one thing today.

shellRuntime.f950: What should I watch out for on a clash day?
shellRuntime.f951: The Horse clashes with the Rat (Zi) in the Zi–Wu clash. On such days accidents while travelling and emotional arguments arise easily, so simply cutting back on rushed schedules and off-the-cuff answers already changes how the day feels.

shellRuntime.f957: The Goat is read as a temperament whose emotional steadiness governs the condition of every other area. On days when the love axis is low, spending time on managing your own feelings before the relationship itself helps the whole day more.
shellRuntime.f958: Can I enter my birth date into this reading?

shellRuntime.f962: When shortcuts lead, trust thins out. Do one thing today the straightforward way.

shellRuntime.f966: How is compatibility decided in the animal reading?
shellRuntime.f967: We use the trines (三合) and clashes (沖) of the twelve branches. The Monkey forms the Water trine with the Rat and the Dragon, and stands in a Yin–Shen clash with the Tiger. These are not arbitrary — they are the basic relationships of Chinese metaphysics.
shellRuntime.f968: You (酉) is the metal of mid-autumn. Those born in the Year of the Rooster have clear standards and finish cleanly. They keep time and keep their word, and a nature that cannot bear disorder carries through into the quality of the result.
shellRuntime.f969: The details are alive. They have the force to keep things running to plan, and they make few mistakes.
shellRuntime.f970: High standards mean frequent corrections, and people drift away. Say what went well first.
shellRuntime.f971: When the day ends, write down one thing you did well. The Rooster's self-scrutiny is strong and needs a counterweight.
shellRuntime.f972: What should a Rooster use a good day for?
shellRuntime.f973: We suggest using it for finishing and checking. The Rooster's strength comes from bringing what already exists to an exact close, rather than from opening something new. Sorting documents, final reviews, and closing accounts suit it well.
shellRuntime.f974: What should I do on a day the reading comes out badly?
shellRuntime.f975: You cannot avoid the day, but you can move the weight. Postponing large decisions in the low-scoring area and filling it with low-load work already changes how the day feels.
shellRuntime.f976: Xu (戌) is the earth of late autumn. Those born in the Year of the Dog have deep loyalty to people and a clear sense of right and wrong. Once they trust someone they hold to it, and they choose principle even at a loss.
shellRuntime.f977: They can be relied on. They are the ones still there in a crisis, and they hold the centre in an organisation.
shellRuntime.f978: Weighing right and wrong can cost you people. Listen once more to the other side's circumstances.
shellRuntime.f979: Write your worries on paper and mark only the ones you can change. The Dog's sense of responsibility is large and easily picks up unnecessary loads.
shellRuntime.f980: Why does the Dog reading talk so much about relationships?
shellRuntime.f981: Xu (戌) is read as the nature that guards and forms a group. For the Dog, what is gained and lost in relationships weighs heavily on the day, so the people axis appears often in the interpretation.
shellRuntime.f982: Which is more accurate, the animal reading or the zodiac reading?
shellRuntime.f983: It is not a question of one being better but of different coordinate systems. The animal uses the branch of your birth year; the zodiac uses the Sun's position along the ecliptic. Putting the two results side by side and looking at where they overlap raises confidence.
shellRuntime.f984: Hai (亥) is the water entering winter. As befits the last of the twelve branches, those born in the Year of the Pig are generous and want little, and they take people in without picking and choosing. That goodwill eventually comes back as fortune.
shellRuntime.f985: Goodwill runs deep around them. What they gave comes back from unexpected quarters, and people gather.
shellRuntime.f986: Not being able to refuse lets losses accumulate. Decline one thing politely today.
shellRuntime.f987: Keep a note of the kindnesses you receive. The Pig's relationships last when giving and receiving stay in balance.
shellRuntime.f988: How should the Pig read the money axis?
shellRuntime.f989: For the Pig, the outcome turns less on earning a lot than on keeping it from leaking. On days when the money axis is low, it is more practical to check whether money is going out because you could not say no, rather than to worry about income.

shellRuntime.f1400: Jiao (角宿) is the horn of the Azure Dragon of the East, the very first of the twenty-seven mansions. Among the seven luminaries it belongs to Wood (木), so it is born with the pioneering force that pushes out first, the way a sprout shoulders the soil aside. Read through gyeokgak, it leads others from the front — and the task of this star is to gather that forwardness into one first spadeful so it does not leak away as haste.
shellRuntime.f1401: Kang (亢宿) is the straight neck of the Azure Dragon, and among the seven luminaries it falls under Metal (金). Principle and self-respect that will not soften, like wrought metal, are this star's frame. But when straightness goes too far the room turns cold, so set your principles and still leave one door in them for people to pass through.
shellRuntime.f1402: Di (氐宿) is the base of the Azure Dragon, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Earth (土). As soil holds and raises all things, this is the star of accumulation that stacks inward and firms the ground. Its grain achieves most when the roots go deep rather than when it hurries, so when impatience rises, look first at the floor you are standing on.
shellRuntime.f1403: Fang (房宿) is the belly of the Azure Dragon, assigned among the seven luminaries to the Sun (日). As the sun lights a whole gathering, this is the star of authority that holds people and leads from the front. That light draws people when it is used as care rather than rule, so lead — and call the name of whoever stands behind you first.
shellRuntime.f1404: Xin (心宿) is the heart of the Azure Dragon, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of the Moon (月). As moonlight reads what is inside the dark, this is the star of intuition that catches even what was not said. But when that sensitivity tips into suspicion you grow lonely on your own, so the stronger the hunch, the more it helps to confirm one fact before you move.
shellRuntime.f1405: Wei (尾宿) is the tail of the Azure Dragon, and among the seven luminaries it enters Fire (火). As flame cuts across a dry field, this is the star of breakthrough that drives through what is blocked. Its resilience is uncommon, but once everything has burned only exhaustion is left — so before you tear something down, decide first on one seed to plant in that spot again.
shellRuntime.f1406: Ji (箕宿) is the winnowing basket at the Azure Dragon's end, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Water (水). As water spreads wide toward low ground, this is the star of freedom that reaches out past boundaries. Its talent for widening is large but scatters easily, so however far you go, keep one harbour to return to in mind.
shellRuntime.f1407: Dou (斗宿) is the first star of the Black Tortoise of the North, assigned among the seven luminaries to Wood (木). As the Big Dipper points out a direction, this is the star of wisdom that tells others the way. When teaching runs ahead as admonition the road closes, so walking the way yourself before putting it into words carries far further.
shellRuntime.f1408: Nu (女宿) is the Weaver Maid of the Black Tortoise, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Earth (土). As one chooses thread strand by strand, this is the star of refinement that finishes by tuning the fine detail. So that an eye set on perfection does not harden into self-scrutiny, we suggest practising with 'done' as the goal rather than a hundred out of a hundred.
shellRuntime.f1409: Xu (虛宿) is the empty seat of the Black Tortoise, and among the seven luminaries it enters the Sun (日). Like the stillness after sundown, this is the star of reflection that looks inward. Emptiness becomes strength in this seat, but sink into it too long and it turns hollow — so after reflecting, always take one step back outside.
shellRuntime.f1410: Wei (危宿) is the cliff of the Black Tortoise, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of the Moon (月). As the moon waxes and wanes, this is the star that handles crisis and turning points boldly. The tighter you grip to control, the further it tips to extremes — so let go of what cannot be changed and gather your force onto the one thing that can.
shellRuntime.f1411: Shi (室宿) is the palace of the Black Tortoise, assigned among the seven luminaries to Fire (火). As one kindles a fire to raise a new house, this is the star of creation that first sets up what did not exist. Its opening force is strong but the finish is easily weak, so this time raise just one window and keep the fire burning to the end.
shellRuntime.f1412: Bi (壁宿) is the wall of the Black Tortoise, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Water (水). As water fills a crack, this is the star of mediation that joins people and settles conflict. When accommodating others costs you your own share, tuning becomes sacrifice — so check the level of your own heart before other people's balance.
shellRuntime.f1413: Kui (奎宿) is the first star of the White Tiger of the West, and among the seven luminaries it enters Wood (木). Like a scholar with brush in hand, this is the star of tradition that finishes with form and dignity. When the rule comes before the person the room turns cold, so drop one formality and lay a warm word in its place.
shellRuntime.f1414: Lou (婁宿) is the White Tiger's binding, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Metal (金). As one weaves thread, this is the star of sociability that links people and widens the circle. Wide but not deep leaves nothing to lean on, so rather than adding new ties, spend more care on the one person you will know for a long time.
shellRuntime.f1415: Wei (胃宿) is the White Tiger's storehouse, assigned among the seven luminaries to Earth (土). As one fills a granary, this is the star of accumulation that gathers resources and plans. Trying to hold everything only grows the unease, so clear out the old at regular intervals and something better takes that place.
shellRuntime.f1416: Mao (昴宿) is the White Tiger's cluster, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of the Sun (日). As many stars gather and shine, this is the star of care that holds and watches over the weaker. Weighing and measuring easily pushes people away, so when judgement runs ahead, hold first and speak later.
shellRuntime.f1417: Bi (畢宿) is the White Tiger's net, and among the seven luminaries it enters the Moon (月). As one weaves a net tight, this is the star of the artisan who completes things quietly. shellRuntime.f1418: Zi (觜宿) is the White Tiger's beak, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Fire (火). Even a true remark becomes an attack when it is sharp, so grow curious before you persuade and speech turns into a bridge rather than a weapon.
shellRuntime.f1419: Shen (參宿) is the White Tiger's hunter, assigned among the seven luminaries to Water (水). When speed outruns people, wounds are left behind — so the harder you push, the more it pays to stop briefly, look at the hearts beside you, and go on.
shellRuntime.f1420: Jing (井宿) is the well of the Vermilion Bird of the South, and among the seven luminaries it enters Wood (木). As well water runs clear, this is the star of reason that puts disorder back in order by principle. When coolness comes first the warmth dries up, so lay one layer of kind words on before you hand down a judgement.
shellRuntime.f1421: Gui (鬼宿) is the Vermilion Bird's gate, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Metal (金). As something seeps through a gap in the door, this is the star of instinct that senses the unseen and looks after people. Its moods run in large waves, so keep your own rhythm before you take others in.
shellRuntime.f1422: Liu (柳宿) is the Vermilion Bird's willow, assigned among the seven luminaries to Earth (土). The tighter you grip the more stifled the other feels, so loosen your hand a little and go long with a looser devotion.
shellRuntime.f1423: Xing (星宿) is the Vermilion Bird's star, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of the Sun (日). Fixating only on winning makes people leave, so stake the contest on one thing and let the names of those below you shine in the rest.
shellRuntime.f1424: Zhang (張宿) is the Vermilion Bird's wing, and among the seven luminaries it enters the Moon (月). shellRuntime.f1425: Yi (翼宿) is the Vermilion Bird's other wing, and among the seven luminaries it holds the seat of Fire (火). As one preens the feathers to finish them, this is the star of quality and courtesy. When correction comes out first the room stiffens, so mind the finish — and say out loud what the other person did well before anything else.
shellRuntime.f1426: Zhen (軫宿) is the carriage of the Vermilion Bird of the South and the last of the twenty-seven mansions. Assigned among the seven luminaries to Water (水), it is the star of closure that sets down neatly what it has carried. Trying to tidy everything perfectly easily postpones the decision, so do not weigh it — finish the one thing in your hand today, for certain.
shellRuntime.f1427: Ashwini is the first star, ruled by Ketu, with the dawn healers the Ashwini Kumaras as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to heal quickly' — a Deva (divine) temperament laid over a Vata (wind) constitution gives it a grain that begins and restores anything at speed. The growth point of this star is practising to carry what it started all the way through, so that hurry does not leave things unfinished.
shellRuntime.f1428: Bharani is ruled by Venus, but its deity is Yama, god of death and rebirth. Its shakti is 'the power to take away and purify' — the star of transformation that sends the old off and lets the new in. A Manushya (human) temperament carries the motive of Artha (achievement), giving it the grit to digest even a burden that looks too heavy to bear.
shellRuntime.f1429: Krittika is ruled by the Sun, with Agni, god of fire, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to burn and purify' — Rakshasa (fierce) concentration meets the motive of Kama (creativity), giving it a sharpness that cuts away impurity without mercy. That fire shines most when it is used to warm others, so do not forget the warmth you hold before you cut.
shellRuntime.f1430: Rohini is ruled by the Moon, with Brahma (Prajapati) the creator as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to make things grow' — Kapha's steadiness blends with the motive of Moksha (spirituality) to draw in material abundance and beauty. It is bright to the pleasures of the senses, and it needs an eye that watches the flow so they do not become attachment.
shellRuntime.f1431: Mrigashira is ruled by Mars, but its deity is Soma, the gentle moon god. Its shakti is 'the power to find fulfilment' — a Deva temperament carries a pure searching spirit, making it a deer-like star always roaming after something. Only when that curiosity meets a resting place does the heart settle.
shellRuntime.f1432: Ardra is ruled by Rahu, with Rudra, god of storms, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to change through effort' — taking a teardrop as its symbol, the grain of this star is the deep empathy that arrives after upheaval. Vata's change meets the motive of Kama, so rather than pushing on, tend to the recovery that follows the storm.
shellRuntime.f1433: Punarvasu is ruled by Jupiter, with Aditi the boundless mother as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to regain abundance' — the star of return that rises again however many times it loses. A Deva temperament carries the motive of Artha, and not losing its optimism is this star's greatest asset.
shellRuntime.f1434: Pushya is ruled by Saturn, but its deity is Brihaspati, the teacher-god of Jupiter. A Deva temperament meets the motive of Dharma (calling), and fullness comes to it from raising and caring for others.
shellRuntime.f1435: Ashlesha is ruled by Mercury, with the serpent deity Naga. Its shakti is 'the power to coil and permeate' — Rakshasa insight meets Kapha depth, making it the mysterious star that sees through the subconscious. That insight shows its true worth when it is used for healing rather than for binding.
shellRuntime.f1436: Magha is ruled by Ketu, with the ancestral Pitrs as its deity. Rakshasa force carries the motive of Artha, and it earns respect in the seat where it guards and continues what was handed down.
shellRuntime.f1437: Purva Phalguni is ruled by Venus, with Bhaga, god of delight, as its deity. shellRuntime.f1438: Uttara Phalguni is ruled by the Sun, with Aryaman, god of contracts and friendship, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to accumulate and prosper' — the star that builds lasting relationships out of trust and generosity. A Manushya temperament meets the motive of Moksha, and the more it gives, the more prosperity returns.
shellRuntime.f1439: Hasta is ruled by the Moon, with Savitr, the creative power of the Sun, as its deity. Its shakti is 'the power to hold what one wants in the hand' — the star of skill and realisation, taking the hand as its symbol. A Deva temperament carries the motive of Moksha, and it draws healing and reward from what it makes with its fingertips.
shellRuntime.f1440: Chitra is a star forged by Mars, with Vishwakarma, the cosmic artisan, as its deity.
